correctness.rationale: The maximal torus standard representation splits into m hyperbolic weight pairs, establishing matching-graph necessity and independence. Conversely, nonorthogonal edges split off orthogonal nondegenerate hyperbolic planes, and the independent remaining isotropic lines extend by Witt to a complete hyperbolic basis. Any failure has either a three-line nonmatching graph or a linearly dependent orthogonal circuit with at most m+1 members by maximal-isotropic rank m. A maximal-isotropic m+1 line circuit realizes sharpness. The toric projective-space dimension is obtained by applying the local and global ray-parabolic compatibility characterization in Proposition 5.1 of arXiv:2610.11340v1. The exact finite rational verification script was replayed successfully from the supplied content; it supports but does not replace the infinite proof.

The known GL_m embedding supplies the m+1 lower bound, which is not claimed as new. value.rationale: The natural isotropic-point maximal-parabolic stratum in type D_m, where the source leaves the full group h(D_m) unresolved, admits a sharp one-unit improvement over the published general m+2 upper bound. The complete forbidden-configuration dichotomy is a structural classification (graph-star versus projective circuit). The corresponding if-and-only-if splitting threshold d>=m+1 for toric principal SO(2m)-bundles on projective space with isotropic-line ray parabolics supplies a directly motivated algebraic-geometric application not derivable merely from the source m+1 lower bound.
